text:
A CPU branch predictor is a small hardware mechanism that guesses which way a conditional branch will go before the branch condition is fully resolved. When the processor encounters a branch instruction, it must decide whether to fetch the next instruction from the “taken” path or the “not taken” path. Making this guess early lets the CPU keep fetching and executing instructions while the branch is still being evaluated, hiding the delay that would otherwise stall the pipeline. If the guess is wrong, the CPU discards the work done along the wrong path and redirects the instruction fetch to the correct address.

The predictor learns from past behavior. Simple predictors track each branch’s recent history using a small table of counters. For example, a two-bit counter can represent “strongly not taken,” “weakly not taken,” “weakly taken,” and “strongly taken,” updating after each
